tools.name: keepwarm
tools.description: Keeps this session's 1-hour prompt cache warm while the user is away: 55 minutes after the last request it sends a tool-less fork of this conversation that is billed at the cache-read rate and adds nothing to the transcript, instead of the user paying a full cache re-write when they come back (e.g. 400K tokens on Opus 5.5: ~$0.10/h warm vs ~$3.20 cold). Call action "start" when you end a turn with a large context (100K+ tokens) and the user will plausibly return to THIS conversation within the next hours: work is mid-way, you are waiting on their review or answer, or they said they will be back. Pick hours to cover that gap (default 3, max 12). Call "stop" when the work is finished, the user is done for the day, or you are about to suggest /clear or a new session. A running window re-arms itself after every turn, so do not call start again each turn; call "status" if unsure. The user's /keepwarm command overrides you: if they turned it off, start is refused. Without a window, an idle check at 50 minutes asks the user whether to compact. If something should be checked while the user is away (a training job, a deploy, a service), pass wake_prompt: at each wake the fork first decides, knowing the time, to skip silently, record a one-line note in this conversation, run a real turn with tools (only then does the conversation grow), or stop.
